llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (a runtime security guard) is plausible, but key behavioral details depend on installing an external plugin package that isn't included here and would store an API key and route sanitized metadata to a cloud service — this combination and the missing provenance make the package worth extra scrutiny before installing.

dimensions.detail: MoltGuard is described as an agent security plugin and the included scripts (activate/status) and docs consistently reference registration with a Core service and local credential storage. That functionality (registering an agent, storing an API key, querying account status) is coherent with a cloud-backed security product. However, the bundle here does not contain the core interception/sanitization code (index.ts and other implementation files are referenced but not present), so the full runtime behavior depends on an external package that the SKILL.md tells the agent to install.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to install an external plugin package and to run activation which will POST to the vendor Core and save credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. It also instructs the agent to read a sample file to demonstrate detection and to relay quota-exceeded messages verbatim. The included scripts only handle registration/status; the SKILL promises real-time interception of tool calls and sending sanitized metadata to Core — that capability is not present in the files here and would be implemented by the external package. Because activation enables cloud communication and persistent credentials, the instructions expand the agent's network and file access scope (potential for sending metadata to a remote service).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec bundled with the registry entry; SKILL.md instructs using 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard', which will download and install code from an external package (npm/registry or similar). The security-relevant behaviors (interception, sanitization, network calls) are implemented by that external package — the registry entry does not include or vet that code. This means installing will execute code obtained over the network that is not part of this skill bundle; you should verify the package provenance before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables. It does, however, create and use a local credentials file (~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json) and will POST to https://www.openguardrails.com/core. Storing a provider API key locally and routing sanitized metadata to a remote Core is proportionate to a cloud-backed security product, but it centralizes access and requires trust that sanitization is effective and that only intended, non-sensitive metadata is transmitted.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and model invocation is allowed (normal). The skill’s activation flow writes persistent credentials to the user's home directory and links agents to a shared account/quota. Persisting an API key and enabling cloud-based classification are legitimate for this product, but they increase the blast radius if the remote service or package is malicious or compromised.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a cloud-backed security plugin and its local scripts (activate/status) are consistent with that. However, the core interception and sanitization code is not included in this bundle — installation will download an external package (@openguardrails/moltguard) which will have the runtime behavior of intercepting tool calls and sending sanitized metadata to openguardrails.com and will store an API key locally. Before installing: 1) verify the package provenance (npm repository.url, GitHub repo, release tarball) and inspect the package contents or run npm pack/diff as described in references/details.md; 2) confirm you trust https://www.openguardrails.com/core and that their sanitization truly removes sensitive data (test in an isolated environment or sandbox and monitor network traffic with a proxy / tcpdump); 3) be aware activation will create ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json containing an API key — treat it as a sensitive secret and remove it if you revoke access; 4) prefer installing in a non-production or restricted environment first and review the external package source code (index.ts, platform-client, sanitizer) before enabling in systems that handle secrets. If you cannot verify the external package provenance and behavior, consider this skill suspicious and avoid installing it.
